bug_semantics: Concurrent action requests execute template rendering in separate ExecRequest goroutines, but the renderer calls Parse on one process-wide *text/template.Template and then executes the returned pointer, which is the same mutated receiver. Interleaved Parse and Execute operations can replace one request's parse tree with another request's tree, contaminate shell commands and arguments across users, or concurrently mutate text/template's internal maps and terminate the service.
flaw_origin: Commit 6b342cbedb041f515a76495cec69f9979bd34d1e first introduced the flawed Go-template mechanism in service/internal/entities/templates.go: a package-level `var tpl = template.New("tpl")`, followed on every rendering call by `t, err := tpl.Parse(source)` and `t.Execute(...)`. ExecRequest already launched each execution through `go func()`, so the new shared mutable template was immediately reachable concurrently. Later moves and refactors, including b37f035ea653e6f238a7cdfa0f636f518a692dc4, b777d599aa1869871d67eb43cf64908d513976ee, 086a5ffd22b41766f5cbe2654a53b2771fe004b7, and 544515c2a6bd44454bbdb86829e5b63da798fd71, preserved or reorganized the mechanism and are not the origin.
ai_marker: absent: the exact commit object for 6b342cbedb041f515a76495cec69f9979bd34d1e has human author and committer `jamesread <contact@jread.com>`, the sole message `chore: Port huge amount of code to OliveTin 3k`, no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, no bot identity, and no other AI-attribution marker.
evidence: The repository's first-party advisory, https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/security/advisories/GHSA-7fq5-7wr8-rjwj, identifies service/internal/tpl/templates.go, the package-level `tpl`, the unsafe `tpl.Parse(source)` then `t.Execute(...)` sequence, the ExecRequest goroutine call chain, cross-request command contamination, and concurrent-map-write denial of service. Its package panel reports affected versions `>= 3000.0.0`; although that panel currently says `Patched versions: None`, the advisory references the security fix and release, and the assigned GitHub advisory API snapshot names pseudo-version `0.0.0-20260521225117-d74da9314005` as first patched.

First-party fix commit https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/commit/d74da9314005954dd49fa20dabf272247bc76519 has parent 276e3f62ddb87f9cb87903b19203e35db01a0c95 and directly changes service/internal/tpl/templates.go: parseTemplate no longer calls `tpl.Parse(source)`; it calls `tpl.Clone()` and parses the per-call clone, so concurrent requests no longer mutate the shared root template.

First-party release https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/releases/tag/3000.13.0 explicitly lists d74da9314005954dd49fa20dabf272247bc76519 under Security for GHSA-7fq5-7wr8-rjwj. The release tag resolves to 8bf52fbea38212e269cbe82f596616b8625a562b.

History search `git log --all -S 'tpl.Parse(source)' -- '*.go'` returns exactly the addition in 6b342cbedb041f515a76495cec69f9979bd34d1e and removal in d74da9314005954dd49fa20dabf272247bc76519. The analogous all-ref search for `var tpl = template.New("tpl")` identifies 6b342cbedb041f515a76495cec69f9979bd34d1e as its origin. `git log -L` follows the singleton through the later entities-to-tpl move and option/function refactors back to that same commit.

The BIC diff creates service/internal/entities/templates.go from /dev/null and writes the vulnerable lines at original lines 12, 77, and 99: the package singleton, `tpl.Parse(source)`, and execution on the returned template. At the same BIC tree, service/internal/executor/executor.go lines 291-294 runs `e.execChain(req)` inside `go func()`, and service/internal/executor/arguments.go line 69 reaches the renderer, establishing the concurrent request path.

Direct-parent-tree verification against 17c716c599b5a11f0bb01d18827014b868a53280 found no Go-tree match for `template.New("tpl")`, `tpl.Parse(source)`, or the `text/template` import; service/internal/entities/templates.go does not exist there, and the BIC creates it from /dev/null. Thus the vulnerable shared-template lines and mechanism are absent in the immediate parent.

Commit 6b342cbedb041f515a76495cec69f9979bd34d1e is a one-parent repository commit. All-ref pickaxe searches expose no smaller member commit for the shared singleton/Parse mechanism; despite its broad port diff, no reconstructable squash-member lineage exists in the validated history, so no decomposition SHA can replace it.

Version ancestry and tree checks establish the boundary: tag 3000.0.0 (45f9c18bc3eed38209f14607de4f6eb7c8bee096) is the first version-sorted release containing the BIC and has `service/internal/entities/templates.go:12: var tpl = template.New("tpl")` and line 77 `tpl.Parse(source)`. Tag 3000.12.0 (3c8490fa5798141f02c2e5fb2cf4c97dc074509b) still has `service/internal/tpl/templates.go:182: t, err := tpl.Parse(source)`. The fix first appears in tag 3000.13.0, where line 184 is `clone, err := tpl.Clone()`; `git tag --contains d74da9314005954dd49fa20dabf272247bc76519` begins at 3000.13.0.

BIC-only AI attribution used `git cat-file -p 6b342cbedb041f515a76495cec69f9979bd34d1e`: tree 55cad3bdcd9c1aeb74550c845f55941554c68f24, sole parent 17c716c599b5a11f0bb01d18827014b868a53280, author and committer jamesread <contact@jread.com>, and only the plain port message. There are no trailers or bot/AI markers in the commit object.
reasoning: The first-party advisory and direct fix agree on the causal defect: Parse mutates a shared text/template receiver, while independent action executions can render concurrently. Vulnerability-first history analysis goes past the current file name and the January 2026 move: the August 2025 commit 6b342cbedb041f515a76495cec69f9979bd34d1e is the smallest available commit that simultaneously introduced the package singleton and per-call Parse/Execute sequence. Its immediate parent lacks the file, import, singleton, and Parse call, while pre-existing executor goroutines make the newly introduced state concurrently reachable. Later commits merely move or refactor those lines. Tag membership places the defect in the first 3000.0.0 release and through 3000.12.0; d74da9314005954dd49fa20dabf272247bc76519 directly fixes it by cloning before Parse and is included beginning with 3000.13.0. Finally, the exact BIC commit object contains only human jamesread author/committer identities and no AI marker, so the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.
